faqs.question: Is "We loved with a love that was more than love" a real Poe quote?
faqs.answer: Yes. It comes from "Annabel Lee", published in 1849, though the line actually begins "But we loved with a love that was more than love". Most sites drop the "But"; keep it if you put Poe's name under the line.

faqs.question: Did Bram Stoker write "I have crossed oceans of time to find you"?
faqs.answer: No. The line does not appear anywhere in the text of Stoker's 1897 novel Dracula. It is usually traced to the 1992 film, so do not sign it with Stoker's name.

faqs.question: Did Poe really say "Sleep, those little slices of death"?
faqs.answer: There is no evidence he did. The phrase appears nowhere in the five-volume Raven Edition of his works, and the Poe Museum in Richmond could not trace it either.

faqs.question: What should I write in a Halloween card for my wife or husband?
faqs.answer: One classic line plus two sentences of your own works best. Try Poe's "Ulalume" opening for an October anniversary, then add something only the two of you would understand.

faqs.question: Are gothic love quotes too dark for a new relationship?
faqs.answer: Some are. Heathcliff's "Be with me always" suits a long marriage, while Keats's faery's child or Dickinson's polite carriage driver read as playful. Avoid poems about a dead lover if your partner is grieving.

faqs.question: How long should a Halloween love note be?
faqs.answer: Short enough to read on one phone screen, since 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone. The median letter on SubhSandesh's miss-you pages is 88 words (214 pages, two months of data), a sensible ceiling for a card.

faqs.question: Which Emily Dickinson poem works for Halloween?
faqs.answer: "Because I could not stop for Death", from the 1890 first series of her poems. Death arrives as a courteous gentleman in a carriage, which reads more charming than grim.

faqs.question: Can I change a classic quote to include my partner's name?
faqs.answer: Yes, but then remove the quotation marks and the author's name. Once you change "his" to "yours" in Brontë's line, it is your sentence inspired by hers, not a quotation.

faqs.question: Is it okay to post these lines on Instagram?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every classic here is from a text published between 1597 and 1890 and long out of copyright, and the original lines were written for this page for readers to use.

faqs.question: Where does a quote go on the SubhSandesh Halloween card?
faqs.answer: Put a classic line in the letter they read by flashlight in the attic, and a short original line in the closing question, which takes up to 60 characters. The card ends with a downloadable 1080×1920 Boo License.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Romantic Halloween Quotes: 10 Verified Classics and 40 Originals

The best romantic Halloween quotes come in two kinds: a short Gothic classic you can attribute exactly, and an original line in your own voice. Here are 10 public-domain lines from Poe, Shakespeare, Emily Brontë, Keats, Rossetti and Dickinson, each checked against a Project Gutenberg edition, plus 40 originals.

Keep it short. On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, and the romantic "I love you" page is the most-viewed template, with 29.7% of all page views. Love notes get read on small screens.

We also checked five famous lines credited to Poe, Stoker or Shelley: three are not in the texts at all, and two come from horror scenes.

## Why do love and death go together on Halloween?

Gothic writing pairs love with death because death is the one test love cannot pass in life, so the poem lets it pass anyway.

Poe said so himself. In "The Philosophy of Composition" (*Graham's Magazine*, April 1846) he called "the death, then, of a beautiful woman" "unquestionably, the most poetical topic in the world", spoken by a bereaved lover. Read it in the [Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore's transcription](https://www.eapoe.org/works/essays/philcomp.htm).

A 2025 study in *Diálogo das Letras*, [Lima's reading of "Annabel Lee"](https://periodicos.apps.uern.br/index.php/DDL/article/view/7061), notes it was Poe's last complete poem, published in 1849 in six stanzas and 41 lines, and argues its force rests on love and death together. Yukari Oda's 2010 article in *Revue LISA*, [Emily Brontë and the Gothic](https://journals.openedition.org/lisa/3496), places Catherine Earnshaw among Gothic heroines and reads Heathcliff's identity as depending on her existence.

## 10 verified public-domain romantic Halloween quotes

Each line keeps the Gutenberg edition's spelling, capitals and dashes.

### 1. Edgar Allan Poe, "Annabel Lee" (1849)

> "But we loved with a love that was more than love—
> I and my ANNABEL LEE—"

Usually trimmed to start at "We". Source: the Raven Edition, [Volume 5 on Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2151).

### 2. Edgar Allan Poe, "Ulalume" (1847)

> "It was night in the lonesome October
> Of my most immemorial year:"

A poem about lost love, and the natural opener for an October anniversary card.

### 3. Edgar Allan Poe, "The Raven" (1845)

> "For the rare and radiant maiden whom the angels name Lenore—"

Write it above her name.

### 4. Edgar Allan Poe, "Introduction" (Poems, 1831)

> "I could not love except where Death
> Was mingling his with Beauty's breath—"

A couplet Poe later dropped, kept in the Raven Edition notes.

### 5. William Shakespeare, *Romeo and Juliet* (first printed 1597)

> "Shall I believe
> That unsubstantial death is amorous;"

Romeo in the tomb: a caption for a vampire couples' costume.

### 6. Emily Brontë, *Wuthering Heights* (1847)

> "Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same;"

Change "his" to "yours" only if you drop the attribution.

### 7. Emily Brontë, *Wuthering Heights* (1847)

> "Be with me always—take any form—drive me mad! only *do* not leave me in this abyss, where I cannot find you!"

Heathcliff to Catherine's ghost; for long marriages, not third dates.

### 8. John Keats, "La Belle Dame sans Merci" (1819)

> "I met a Lady in the Meads
> Full beautiful, a faery's child,"

A supernatural meet-cute, if you stop before the ending.

### 9. Christina Rossetti, "Remember" (1862)

> "Remember me when I am gone away,
> Gone far away into the silent land;"

Good for long distance.

### 10. Emily Dickinson, "Because I could not stop for Death" (1890)

> "Because I could not stop for Death,
> He kindly stopped for me;"

Death as a polite gentleman caller.

## Which famous "Poe" and "Dracula" love quotes are fake?

We searched all five Raven Edition volumes, *Dracula* (1897) and *Frankenstein* (1818), then checked the Poe Museum's list, [Did Poe Really Say That?](https://poemuseum.org/did-poe-really-say-that/), which says most circulating Poe quotes are misattributed. Skip these:

- **"Sleep, those little slices of death—how I loathe them."** Zero matches. The Poe Museum could not trace it; *A Nightmare on Elm Street 3* credited it to Poe.
- **"I have crossed oceans of time to find you."** Absent from Stoker's novel; usually traced to the 1992 film.
- **"The best things in life make you sweaty."** The Poe Museum says it is not his.
- **"Words have no power to impress the mind with the exquisite horror of their reality."** Genuine Poe, but from chapter 12 of *Arthur Gordon Pym* (1838), where starving sailors drink a shipmate's blood.
- **"I will be with you on your wedding-night!"** Genuine Mary Shelley, but it is the creature's threat.

## 40 original romantic Halloween lines, sorted by use

Every line below was written for this page; swap in names and years.

### Card and letter lines (9)

- October nights get longer, and I'm glad: more of them with you.
- I'd stay in a haunted house if you were the ghost on the stairs.
- You are the candle inside my jack-o'-lantern: the reason any of it glows.
- I'd walk any dark lane on 31 October if it ended at your door.
- Masks come off at midnight. Mine came off the day I met you.
- Of all the spells I know, the one that worked was saying your name.
- Some love stories end at the graveyard gate. Ours just goes in for a moonlit walk.
- You make the dark feel like a blanket instead of a threat.
- I love you by candlelight, in fog, on a plain Tuesday, and most of all on 31 October.

### Caption lines (8)

- Two pumpkins, one porch light.
- Haunting the same house since [year].
- My favourite ghost story is the one where you stayed.
- Bewitched, and not asking for a cure.
- Costumes change. The co-star doesn't.
- Candlelit, cobwebbed, completely smitten.
- Three pumpkins, one black cat, two very soft hearts.
- Scared of everything except how much I love you.

### Text message lines (8)

- Thinking about you more than a Wednesday strictly requires.
- Saved you the last peanut-butter cup. That's how you know it's serious.
- If I vanish tonight, check your arms first.
- Come home soon; the house is too quiet without your footsteps on the stairs.
- You're the only scare I ever wanted: the one where my heart skips.
- Leaving the porch light on for you. Always.
- Halloween plan: you, me, the scariest film we can find, and your hand to grab.
- The candles are lit and the sweets are hidden. Only one thing missing: you.

### Anniversary-in-October lines (7)

- [Number] Octobers together, and the leaves still fall for you the way I did.
- We met in the season of ghosts, and nothing about you has ever faded.
- Happy anniversary to my favourite haunting: the one that never leaves.
- An anniversary and Halloween in one month: two reasons to light every candle.
- Another October of choosing your door over every other.
- Year [number] of being bewitched. Renewal requested.
- If love could carve itself into a pumpkin, ours would light the whole street.

### Long-distance lines (8)

- Different time zones, same Halloween, same me: yours.
- Tonight I'm the ghost at your shoulder, whispering that I miss you.
- The distance is the scariest thing about this Halloween, and it still can't scare me off.
- Light a candle at nine your time. I'll light mine at the same moment.
- Not haunting your house this year, just your phone. Expect me.
- Every jack-o'-lantern on my street looks like it's waiting for you.
- Wear something warm tonight. I can't be your blanket this year.
- One day we'll trick-or-treat on the same street. Until then, this.

## Where should a romantic Halloween quote go?

Put it in writing, where it gets read twice. In [Floyd and colleagues' two randomised trials in *Human Communication Research* (2007)](https://academic.oup.com/hcr/article-abstract/33/2/119/4210722), students who wrote about their affection for someone for 20 minutes on three occasions over five weeks saw significant drops in total cholesterol. We read only the abstract; the full text is paywalled.

| Where it goes | Which kind fits | Length to aim for | SubhSandesh data point |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text message | One original line | 1–2 lines | 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone |
| Card or letter | One classic plus two lines of yours | Under 88 words | Median miss-you letter: 88 words (n=214) |
| Instagram Story | One caption line | Under 10 words | Boo License card: 1080×1920, Story size |
| Interactive page | Classic in the letter, original as the question | Question up to 60 characters | Pages average 11.1 views each |

The 88-word median covers 214 miss-you pages from the two months after that template launched on 28 July 2026, so it is not a Halloween figure; views count opens, not unique visitors.

For one person, the [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) gives the quote a stage. They knock three times on a little haunted house, carve a jack-o'-lantern until your word glows, and read your letter by flashlight in a dark attic: put the Poe or Brontë line there. The closing question defaults to "Will you be my boo?" and takes up to 60 characters. You're emailed when they first answer.

For a longer letter, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) allows 3,000 characters and a 60-second voice note. For a partner in another city, the [miss-you page](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) adds "open when" letters and a reunion countdown.

## When a romantic Halloween quote is the wrong choice

Skip the death-and-love classics when your person is grieving or seriously ill: "Annabel Lee" and "Remember" are about a lover who has died.

If you'll be in the same room on 31 October, a handwritten card beats any page. The Halloween card is English-only, built for one person rather than a party, and will not find you a date. On SubhSandesh 90.9% of started pages get published and shared, but that is no reason to send one where paper is warmer.

- Oda, Y. (9 March 2010). [Emily Brontë and the Gothic](https://journals.openedition.org/lisa/3496). *Revue LISA/LISA e-journal*.

failed.item: No source passes the **swap test** — none could sit unchanged in a different keyword's post in this batch
failed.why: Floyd et al. 2007 (affectionate writing lowers total cholesterol) is about writing affection down in general, so it could sit unchanged in any love-letter or girlfriend/boyfriend post in this batch. It earns its place here only because the post argues quotes belong in writing; the other five sources (Poe 1846 essay, Lima 2025 on Annabel Lee, Oda 2010 on Wuthering Heights, the Poe Museum misattribution list, the Raven Edition text) are specific to this keyword. Closes if an open-access study of quotation or literary-allusion use in romantic messages is found to replace it; searched 'love letters romantic relationships', 'expressing affection in writing health', 'affectionate writing stress Floyd' via findpapers.mjs without one.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this page over the five analysed: it is the only one that verifies its classic quotes against the source texts, and it documents that lines the top results print (the 'Dracula' oceans-of-time line, untrimmed 'Annabel Lee', a reworded Brontë line) are fake or altered, plus first-party sizing data no competitor has. It cannot overcome Pinterest and retailer domain authority, and the 40 original lines compete with hundreds of similar lists; ranking, if it comes, will take months.
